title: Independent literature frontier evidence log — internal research support, not submission prose
coverage_statement: Six independent search routes; targeted frontier audit, not a PRISMA systematic review or claim of exhaustive coverage. Primary sources only support substantive entries. Abstract-only entries are explicitly restricted.

sources.title: Improving Online Job Advertisement Analysis via Compositional Entity Extraction
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata; targeted full-text reading §§1–4, Table 1, §2.3, §3.2, appendix IAA tables; not a claim to read every appendix.
sources.supports: 500 German ads, double annotation plus third curation; tools/objects, alternatives and urgency already modeled; AI application uses around 19,000 ads. Table 3 urgency denominator includes only chains with urgency relations.
sources.difference: Current fixed-task Q shares and unknown-assignment firm-comparison bounds are a different estimand; relational extraction itself is not novel. GOJA's AI optionality figures cannot be compared directly with Q/B.

sources.title: Deep Learning-based Computational Job Market Analysis: A Survey on Skill Extraction and Classification from Job Postings
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract and PDF introduction/search methodology returned by search.
sources.supports: Terminology and dataset heterogeneity are established problems; survey covers neural extraction work before November 2023.
sources.difference: Useful backward-citation map, not evidence that current labels are valid.

sources.title: SkillSpan: Hard and Soft Skill Extraction from English Job Postings
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata and abstract; PDF opening search result. Detailed guideline not read.
sources.supports: An established English span-extraction benchmark is available.
sources.difference: A baseline for span detection, not a direct validator of unconditional qualification operators.

sources.title: Rethinking Skill Extraction in the Job Market Domain using Large Language Models
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract and metadata only.
sources.supports: Six uniformized benchmarks; abstract reports complex-mention advantages without overall superiority to supervised models.
sources.difference: Does not justify treating second-model agreement as human gold-standard accuracy.

sources.title: Skill Requirements across Firms and Labor Markets: Evidence from Job Postings for Professionals
sources.read_scope: NBER author working-paper metadata/abstract and published-version listing; direct full PDF attempts 403.
sources.supports: Within-occupation firm skill heterogeneity and relationships with pay/performance are established.
sources.difference: Current project has no matched wage/productivity outcomes and cannot claim those channels from local expression differences.

sources.title: Upskilling: Do Employers Demand Greater Skill When Workers Are Plentiful?
sources.read_scope: Author preprint pp. 1–6, motivation, identification overview, data introduction; final DOI cross-checked bibliographically.
sources.supports: Advertised education/experience standards respond to labor availability; within firm×title design and external supply shock distinguish composition from changed standards.
sources.difference: One purposive cross-section cannot distinguish supply response, job mix and production demand.

sources.title: Do Recessions Accelerate Routine-Biased Technological Change? Evidence from Vacancy Postings
sources.read_scope: AEA article metadata and abstract.
sources.supports: Persistent skill-requirement changes are studied alongside capital investment and economic shocks.
sources.difference: Provides a competing economic mechanism; does not validate current text states or a causal firm ranking.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence and Jobs: Evidence from Online Vacancies
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract/metadata and author-PDF search opening only.
sources.supports: AI-related establishment demand and aggregate employment effects need distinct scales of analysis.
sources.difference: Current snapshot concerns expressed qualifications; cannot be recast as employment displacement or firm adoption effects.

sources.title: The Diffusion of New Technologies
sources.read_scope: AEA 2024-12-26 author PDF introduction and technology-job data section; human-audit table from NBER revision; publisher issue metadata and final-paper audit excerpt. Versions explicitly distinguished.
sources.supports: Human audit distinguishes company description vs task and use vs production; trimming first/last 50 words is tested. Semantic context validation already exists in economics.
sources.difference: Current candidate-qualification/operator construct is narrower; use document-zone and trimming baselines without claiming the entire distinction is unprecedented.

sources.title: Skill requirements in job advertisements: A comparison of skill-categorization methods based on wage regressions
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata, highlights and abstract; preprint abstract differs in model set/results and is not silently substituted.
sources.supports: Measures can be compared using external wage-explanatory criteria, with interpretability tradeoffs.
sources.difference: Current semantic fidelity needs human/source validation; greater wage R² alone would not prove correct modifier scope.

sources.title: Skill demand versus skill use: Comparing job posts with individual skill use on the job
sources.read_scope: Publisher introduction/conclusion via search; final published PDF pp. 1–2 plus repository cover metadata. Online 12 Dec 2024; issue Jan 2025.
sources.supports: Links Danish job posts to individual survey skill use; reports extensive-margin correspondence but distinct information from intensity.
sources.difference: Useful counterweight to overclaiming ads are uninformative. Current GENERAL/REQUIRED wording is not frequency/intensity of actual skill use.

sources.title: Opening the Black Box of the Matching Function: The Power of Words
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract/metadata; older working-paper opening read but final claims use publisher abstract.
sources.supports: Job-title heterogeneity matters within detailed occupations; senior/manager titles differ in worker-quality returns.
sources.difference: Justifies title/seniority common-support diagnostics, not causal adjustment with sparse cells.

sources.title: Earnings Dynamics, Changing Job Skills, and STEM Careers
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract and metadata only.
sources.supports: Changing occupational skill content and experience/obsolescence have a developed labor-economics framework.
sources.difference: Cross-sectional seniority mix is not a direct measure of obsolescence or career trajectories.

sources.title: Skill demand and labour market concentration: evidence from Italian vacancies
sources.read_scope: Author research page confirms citation; institutional abstract; publisher DOI open blocked. Third-party mirrored text was not used to infer unread methods.
sources.supports: IJM precedent connects advertised skill measures to a labor-market question about concentration and training.
sources.difference: Shows why a substantive economic question is needed; present data lack a market frame for concentration estimation.

sources.title: Partial identification of probability distributions with misclassified data
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract/metadata; Cornell 2005 working-paper abstract, introduction and equation (1.1); not a claim to verify every theorem or final-version proof.
sources.supports: Misclassification restrictions/validation information can define identification regions using the relation between latent and observed distributions.
sources.difference: Current unknown-only intervals protect only flagged U. New error budgets for P/Z are sensitivity assumptions unless independently validated.

sources.title: Text as Data: The Promise and Pitfalls of Automatic Content Analysis Methods for Political Texts
sources.read_scope: Publisher-hosted final PDF pp. 267–269; introduction and validation road map.
sources.supports: Automated text methods require problem-specific validation and do not replace close reading.
sources.difference: Arithmetic reproducibility and second-LLM agreement are separate from construct validity.

sources.title: Toward a framework for creating trustworthy measures with supervised machine learning for text
sources.venue: Political Science Research and Methods, First View, 1–17
sources.read_scope: Publisher HTML §§1,3,5,6, metadata; not all application tables.
sources.supports: Separate validation of labels, model and final measure; LLM prompts/settings, held-out expert comparison and confusion matrices matter.
sources.difference: Can structure a staged validation plan; recommendations are not evidence existing project passed those checks.

sources.title: How well do online job postings match national sources in large English speaking countries?: Benchmarking Lightcast data against statistical sources across regions, sectors and occupations
sources.read_scope: OECD abstract and metadata; not country appendix tables.
sources.supports: Representativeness varies across country, region, industry and occupation; regional agreement is generally better.
sources.difference: A purposive embodied-AI firm sample cannot gain population representativeness just by expanding ad counts.

sources.title: Job descriptions, from conception to recruitment: A qualitative review of hiring processes
sources.venue: JRC Working Papers on Labour, Education and Technology 2022/06
sources.read_scope: JRC official abstract and metadata only; interviews not independently read.
sources.supports: Fourteen HR-professional interviews report heterogeneity by job profile, seniority and firm size, and tool/method-based articulation of competences.
sources.difference: Motivates a testable disclosure/authoring mechanism; cannot assign that mechanism to Galbot or XSquare without evidence.

sources.title: The professional lens: what online job advertisements can say about occupational task profiles
sources.venue: JRC Working Papers on Labour, Education and Technology 2021/13
sources.read_scope: JRC repository abstract/metadata; date follows repository 2021-08-30, while overview page cites 2022.
sources.supports: Compares over 60m UK ads with a survey task database and describes occupation/task-content bias.
sources.difference: Provides a representativeness diagnostic model; current within-task comparison controls only one source of composition.

sources.title: A unified conceptual framework of tasks, skills and competences
sources.venue: JRC Working Papers on Labour, Education and Technology 2021/02
sources.read_scope: JRC repository abstract/metadata, dated 2021-02-09; overview page cites 2022.
sources.supports: Distinguishes tasks as work units, skills as task abilities, and competence across domains.
sources.difference: Named technology, task, qualification expression and actual competence must remain distinct.

sources.title: Methodological issues related to the use of online labour market data
sources.read_scope: ILO HTML abstract, introduction, methods, initial online-data section; not whole reference/annex.
sources.supports: Question/design adaptation, bias analysis and mixed methods are legitimate responses to nonrepresentative online data.
sources.difference: Supports a finite-corpus exploratory design without pretending population inference.

excluded_or_unverified_leads.title: Preparing Job Posting Data for Management Research: A Reproducible Pipeline for Job Analytics
excluded_or_unverified_leads.reason: 2026 proceedings abstract found but full author list/methods not verified; not treated as a full substantive benchmark.

excluded_or_unverified_leads.title: Artificial Intelligence and Skills: Evidence from Contrastive Learning in Online Job Vacancies
excluded_or_unverified_leads.reason: Recent preprint search lead only; no design verification; no causal claims adopted.

excluded_or_unverified_leads.title: Nonparametric Bounds on Treatment Effects
excluded_or_unverified_leads.reason: Foundational bibliographic lead; no primary full text successfully inspected in this audit; no theorem attributed from unread text.
